AboutPage.defaultBody:
JTPA (Japanese Technology Professionals Association) is a community of Japanese technology professionals centered around the Bay Area. We host meetups focused on AI and machine learning, networking events, and project sharing by members.

# What we do

- Regular offline and online study sessions
- Lightning talks from community presenters
- Sharing AI products and projects built by members

HelpPage.title: Help
HelpPage.intro: A guide to JTPA site features. If you have a question, <qaLink>post it in Questions</qaLink>.

signin.title: Account and login
paragraphs: Use Log in in the top-right corner to sign in with a Google account. JTPA does not use email/password registration.
items: Your profile is created automatically on first login from your Google name, icon, and email address.
Login is required for event RSVPs, submissions, comments, likes, and Ask Everyone responses.
To log out, open your account menu in the top-right corner and choose Log out.

events.title: Join events

steps.title: Find an event
steps.body: lists upcoming events, with past events below.

steps.title: RSVP from the detail page
steps.body: Open the event detail page and choose Join. You can register as an attendee or presenter, and answer event-specific questions when provided.

steps.title: Review or cancel your RSVP
steps.body: shows your event history and upcoming registrations. You can cancel from the same screen.

events.callout: Some events are members-only or have capacity limits. If an event is full, waitlisted users are promoted automatically when seats open.

steps.title: RSVP as a presenter
steps.body: Choose the presenter role in the RSVP form and enter your presentation title and abstract.

steps.title: Upload slides or links
steps.body: After RSVPing, use the presentation materials section to add PDF slides or external links such as YouTube. Multiple materials are supported.

steps.title: Update materials later
steps.body: You can replace or add materials from the same section. Published materials are visible on the event page.

showcase.title: Share a project
paragraphs: Share AI projects, services, and tools you built with the community in <showcaseLink>Projects</showcaseLink>. Finished work, prototypes, and work in progress are all welcome.

steps.title: Create a submission
steps.body: opens the submission form. Title, description, and app URL are required; images, tags, repository URL, and demo video URL are optional.

steps.title: Wait for admin review
steps.body: Submissions are saved as pending. Once approved, they appear on the Projects page.

steps.title: Edit your project
steps.body: lets you edit your own projects. Edits move approved projects back to pending for another review.

blog.title: Write articles
paragraphs: Publish articles for the community, such as AI experiences, tutorials, or short essays.

steps.title: Create an article
steps.body: opens the editor. Markdown tables, code blocks, and task lists are supported, along with cover images and tags.

steps.title: Save a draft or request review
steps.body: Save work as a draft, or submit it as pending so an admin can review it.

steps.title: Publish
steps.body: Approved articles appear in <blogLink>Articles</blogLink>. Published articles can be edited and resubmitted without changing the original publish date.

qa.title: Post questions
paragraphs: Questions is for short questions, advice, tips, troubleshooting notes, and observations. Posts are published immediately without admin review.
items: Browse the latest posts from <qaListLink>Questions</qaListLink>.
Create a post from <qaLink>new question</qaLink>. Markdown is supported.
Use comments for answers and follow-up replies.
Edit your own questions from <myQaLink>My Questions</myQaLink>.

guide.title: Read and write notes
paragraphs: <guideListLink>Notes & Know-how</guideListLink> collects AI tool setup notes, prompts people tried, and practical patterns worth finding later. Short notes are welcome too.
items: Anyone can submit from <guideNewLink>new notes and know-how</guideNewLink>.
First-time notes are published after admin review. Once approved, contributor access is granted automatically so future notes can be published directly.
Check your drafts, published notes, and rejected submissions from <myGuidesLink>My Notes & Know-how</myGuidesLink>.
Articles vs. notes: Use articles for longer stories and reflections; use notes and know-how for reusable steps, setup notes, and reference material.

comments.title: Comments and likes
paragraphs: Articles, Notes & Know-how, Questions, Projects, and Ask Everyone detail pages include comments and like buttons.
items: Comments: up to 2000 plain-text characters.
Replies: one level deep and displayed in a flat timeline.
Edit and delete: You can edit or delete your own comments. Deleted comments keep the author and deleted state visible.
Likes: toggled on posts and individual comments.
See <myLikesLink>likes received</myLikesLink> on your comments.

roles.title: Role model
paragraphs: Signed-in users can have admin, editor, contributor, or a combination of those roles. They are stored as Firebase Auth custom claims and take effect after the user signs in again.

cells: Full access to events, projects, articles, attendees, notes and know-how, About, and user role management.
Create, edit, publish, and delete all notes and know-how, including submissions written by other users.
Publish, edit, and delete their own notes without review.
Regular member: RSVP, submit content, comment, like, and submit first-time notes for admin review.

roles.callout: editor and contributor are subsets of admin. If an editor opens a restricted /admin page directly, they are redirected to /admin/guides (exceptions: Notes & Know-how management and this help page). contributor access does not grant /admin access; it only allows self-publishing the user's own notes.

steps.title: Create a draft
steps.body: creates a new draft. You can also click Clone on an existing row in <adminEventsLink>/admin/events</adminEventsLink> to use a past event as the starting point (date becomes today + 7 days; RSVP/presentation subcollections are not copied).

steps.title: Configure survey questions
steps.body: Optionally add key + label + type + audience pairs. The audience can be everyone or presenters only. Presenter-only questions appear only to users who RSVP as presenters.

steps.title: Set visibility
steps.body: Choose public or members-only visibility. Members-only events are hidden from the /events list for signed-out visitors.

steps.title: Move status to published
steps.body: Changing status from draft to published shows the event in the public event list.

steps.title: Collect presenter materials
steps.body: Presenters upload slide or video links from the presenter section on /events/[slug]. A presenter can attach multiple materials to one event.

steps.title: Wrap up after the event
steps.body: After the event end time, it is treated as past automatically (the RSVP form is hidden and the event moves to Past events on /events). If you also want the admin view to show it as past, change status to past.

attendees.title: Attendees and CSV export
paragraphs: <adminAttendeesQueryLink>/admin/attendees?eventId=...</adminAttendeesQueryLink> (or the event selector) shows attendees and survey responses.
items: Copy emails: copies confirmed attendee emails as a comma-separated list. Paste it into Gmail BCC to expand individual recipients.
Download CSV: UTF-8 BOM CSV that opens directly in Excel. Columns include displayName, affiliation, email, role, status, presentationTitle, presentationAbstract, survey_key...
Filter: defaults to confirmed attendees only. Switch to all when you need canceled or waitlisted registrations.
Details: open Details on each row to review survey responses.
attendees.callout: Gmail Web can hit limits around bulk sends above ~500 recipients. Use the existing JTPA Google Group (about 2,000 members) or wait for the Trigger Email + Cloud Functions implementation planned in issue #15.

projects.title: Project review

steps.title: Open the pending list
steps.body: shows unapproved projects at the top.

steps.title: Review the submission
steps.body: Use the Open app link to inspect the actual app. The author, tags, and screenshots are shown as context.

steps.title: Approve or reject
steps.body: Add a rejection comment when needed. Approval immediately publishes the project to <showcaseLink>/showcase</showcaseLink>.

projects.note: Authors can edit their own submissions from /my/projects. Editing an approved project automatically returns status to pending, so another review is required.

posts.title: Article review
paragraphs: <adminPostsLink>/admin/posts</adminPostsLink> is organized into four sections: pending review, published, draft, and rejected.
items: Cover image previews, excerpts, and tags are shown.
Preview opens the public detail page; Edit content lets an admin directly fix typos or wording.
Approval publishes immediately. publishedAt is set only on first publication and is preserved on republish.
Rejection comments are queued for author notification (sent once the Trigger Email extension is enabled; currently they only accumulate in the queue).

guides.title: Notes review and contributor grants
paragraphs: /admin/guides manages AI tool explainers, setup notes, and reusable know-how. It is the only admin page that editor users can also edit.
Community notes and know-how submissions appear at the top as pending. Each card supports preview, edit, comments, and the Publish or Reject decision.

steps.title: Preview or edit content
steps.body: Review what the author wrote. If typo fixes are needed, it is fine to edit from the admin side before publishing (editors use the same flow).

steps.title: Optionally add a comment
steps.body: Add feedback when rejecting. Approval comments are not included in email.

steps.title: Publish and grant contributor
steps.body: Publishing the note also grants the author the contributor: true custom claim automatically, so future notes no longer need review. The author must sign out and sign in again before the role becomes active.

steps.title: Reject
steps.body: Reject with a comment. The author can read the reason from /my/guides, revise, and resubmit.

items: The order field controls display order on /guide (ascending). Only admins and editors can change it.
Draft (draft) and published (published) notes can be edited from the same admin page.
Markdown supports GFM tables, code blocks, and task lists; code is syntax-highlighted.
If someone abuses contributor access, downgrade them from <adminUsersLink>/admin/users</adminUsersLink> with Revoke contributor. Existing published notes remain published.

about.title: Editing About JTPA
paragraphs: /admin/about edits the title and Markdown body for /about. Until content is saved, the page uses the default copy from code.
about.note: Headings are lowered one level automatically (H1 -> H2 ...), so using # in the body is safe.

users.title: Users and roles
paragraphs: <adminUsersLink>/admin/users</adminUsersLink> lists all users with last login time and current roles.
items: You can grant or revoke editor and admin roles.
Removing admin from yourself, or removing the last remaining admin, is rejected for safety.
Role changes take effect only after the user signs in again because claims must propagate through the session cookie and client state.
Users who have never signed in do not appear in the list, so roles cannot be pre-granted there.
users.callout: If the UI is unavailable, see the Granting roles (CLI fallback) section in <docsAdminLink>docs/admin.md</docsAdminLink>.

deploy.title: Deployment checks
paragraphs: A push to the main branch automatically builds and deploys through Firebase App Hosting (about 2-3 minutes).
items: Progress: <rolloutsLink>App Hosting Rollouts</rolloutsLink>
Production error logs: <cloudLogsLink>Cloud Run Logs</cloudLogsLink>
If production errors appear, you can roll back to the previous release because the older Cloud Run image is still available.
